title: Kitchen and Songbook
premise: Ines Yarrow has built a career on erasure, ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrity chef Marguerite Vale while keeping her own name off every page. When a letter Ines wrote eleven years ago — never sent, addressed to her first love, composer Tal Okafor — surfaces in Marguerite's archive of purchased secrets, Ines realizes Marguerite has been weaponizing her past to control her. As Ines and Tal are thrown together restoring a family songbook and kitchen that both their families once shared, Ines must decide whether to expose Marguerite at the cost of the career that rescued her from poverty. The novel ends with Ines publishing under her own name for the first time, burning the ghostwriting contract, and choosing Tal — not as a return to the past, but as a present finally claimed.
about_author: Beatrix Sandoval is the pen name of a former restaurant line cook who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming her own. She lives in a coastal town where she collects secondhand songbooks and cooks for people she loves.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines ghostwrites the final chapters of Marguerite Vale's memoir in Marguerite's gleaming test kitchen, invisible among the staff who assume she's an assistant. Establishes her talent for vanishing into others' voices. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort and cost of being unseen.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. While cataloging Marguerite's private archive for 'research,' Ines finds her own unsent letter to Tal, bought from a memorabilia dealer. Her handwriting stares back at her like a stranger's. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past she sealed has been someone's possession all along.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Wants
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite reveals she knows Ines wrote the letter and dangles it as leverage: finish the memoir exactly as dictated, or the letter — and Ines's authorship of Marguerite's most intimate passages — goes public. Emotional beat: cold power dressed as generosity; the reader sees Marguerite's corruption clearly.

chapters.title: The Songbook on the Shelf
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Hunting provenance for the letter, Ines traces it to a decommissioned music school where Tal now teaches, and learns he's restoring a shared family songbook — one containing songs her grandmother wrote. Emotional beat: reluctant gravity pulling toward the past tense she swore off.

chapters.title: Tal
chapters.summary: Tal's POV. Tal recognizes Ines instantly but pretends, for one afternoon, not to, letting them work side by side over the songbook. He remembers the letter she never sent and wonders why she's here now. Emotional beat: tenderness held carefully, like a note sustained too long.

chapters.title: Terms of Erasure
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines signs a tightened NDA making her legally Marguerite's voice, even as she begins secretly meeting Tal. Each lie to Marguerite sharpens her sense of her own complicity. Emotional beat: the thrill of deception curdling into self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Recipes and Refrains
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ines and Tal cook and transcribe their grandmothers' shared recipes and songs, discovering the two women were collaborators erased by history — one credited, one not. The parallel to Ines's life lands hard. Emotional beat: inheritance as both wound and invitation.

chapters.title: The Memoir of Someone Else
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marguerite demands Ines write a fabricated childhood scene portraying herself as the wronged party in an old rivalry with Tal's family. Ines recognizes the lie because she's living inside its structure. Emotional beat: horror at how fluently she can falsify a soul.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: Tal's POV. Tal asks directly what happened eleven years ago; Ines gives him the polished, evasive version. Later, alone, she drafts the truth of why she left — ambition, shame, his family's collapse — and deletes it. Emotional beat: love deferred by habit, honesty rehearsed and abandoned.

chapters.title: Archive Fire
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A rival biographer leaks that Marguerite's memoir contains ghostwritten fabrications; Marguerite blames Ines and accelerates her threats, moving up publication. Ines realizes Marguerite will burn everything, including her, to control the narrative. Emotional beat: rising dread, the walls of the contract closing in.

chapters.title: The Letter Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Tal's POV. Marguerite, sensing Tal's leverage, invites him to the estate and lets him read Ines's letter — her unguarded words about loving him. Tal arrives at Ines's door holding it. Emotional beat: exposure without consent; intimacy weaponized by a third hand.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Late
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered, Ines finally tells Tal the whole truth: why she left, why she never sent the letter, what Marguerite holds over her. Tal's anger is quiet and worse than shouting — he grieves the years, not the confession. Emotional beat: rupture that is also release.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers annotations in the songbook in her grandmother's hand — corrections, claims of authorship — evidence that could restore her grandmother's credit and expose Marguerite's family's theft. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as scholarship.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite offers Ines co-credit, money, and protection if she delivers the songbook and buries the marginalia — and hints she'll destroy Tal's school's funding if refused. We see Marguerite genuinely believe she's being fair. Emotional beat: corruption convinced of its own virtue.

chapters.title: What the Career Saved
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines audits her life: the apartment, her mother's medical debts paid, her brother's tuition — all built on silence. She drafts two resignation letters, one cowardly, one true. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of gratitude toward something corrupt.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Tal's POV. Tal performs the restored songbook publicly, crediting both grandmothers, and afterward tells Ines he doesn't want her back unless she comes as herself — named, visible, unfinished. Emotional beat: love as a demand for wholeness, not rescue.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Publication day approaches; Marguerite's lawyers confirm the letter goes to press unless Ines complies fully. Ines photographs the marginalia, copies the archives, and sends everything to the biographer and a journalist — knowing there's no undoing it. Emotional beat: the calm after the irreversible decision.

chapters.title: Conflagration
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The exposé detonates: fabrication, stolen songs, ghostwritten intimacies. Marguerite retaliates by publishing the letter and outing Ines as her ghost — but the public reads the letter as evidence of Ines's humanity, not scandal. Emotional beat: climax; ruin and vindication arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Named
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In the fallout, Ines publishes her own account — her name on the cover for the first time — telling the truth about everyone, including herself. Marguerite's empire fractures; Ines loses contracts and sleep and regrets nothing. Emotional beat: grief and freedom indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Kitchen They Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, Ines and Tal reopen the old school kitchen for community suppers, cooking the corrected recipes, singing the corrected songs. The work is small and real. Emotional beat: quiet repair; inheritance reclaimed as practice, not property.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines writes Tal a new letter and hands it to him unsealed, then says the words aloud — no past tense, no intermediary, no ghost. He answers in kind. Emotional beat: vulnerability chosen freely; the arc of hiding completed and reversed.

chapters.title: Coda: First Edition
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. At a bookstore reading, Ines signs her own name beside Tal's in a copy of the restored songbook. Marguerite's memoir is remaindered; theirs is in its first printing. Emotional beat: resolution — identity kept, power refused, inheritance shared.
